summary: Improve team work design, knowledge transfer and age-inclusive leadership. Explore the five-day course and practical team exercises.
lede: Leading multigenerational teams involves helping supervisors and people professionals coordinate work across age groups without relying on age-based assumptions. This foundation-level course is for team leaders, line managers and people professionals who allocate work, develop talent or support collaboration. You will map team skills, check assumptions in work and development decisions, and use reverse mentoring, conflict discussion and a team charter to support knowledge exchange and inclusive ways of working.
audienceIntro: This foundation-level course is designed for people who allocate work, develop talent or support day-to-day collaboration across age-diverse teams. It is relevant when your role includes coaching colleagues, addressing age-related assumptions or retaining important team knowledge.
modules: WHO Ageism Evidence and Bias Checks
Job Demands-Resources Model and Work Design
Team Charter and Age-Inclusive Action Plan
prerequisites: No specialist knowledge of age-inclusive management frameworks is assumed. Experience supervising, coordinating or contributing to a workplace team will help you apply the exercises.
